title: How many first-time employers a Columbus payroll company's 2027 plan should count on across twelve states, when three states' online formation filings started filing the IRS employer number application for businesses that tick the box
subdomain: forecasting-forecast-evaluation (employer business formation forecast from business applications when a filing reform changed who applies: the added applications' formation yield identified against the states the reform did not reach, before and after)
prompt_shape: a committed plan figure to the nearest 100, a table by sales territory of the 2024 first-time employers (signed, still with us in the fourth quarter of 2025, gross wages in their first quarter on payroll to the cent), a table of the 2024 first-time employers by signup channel, and a one-page note with a chart of each territory's signed against still with us

sources.origin: constructed for this task by task163/generator/build.py (seeded, deterministic) around a fictional payroll services company in Columbus, Ohio. The three statistics files follow the layouts of the Census Bureau's Business Formation Statistics API and monthly download and the Census Nonemployer Statistics API, but every value in them is simulated for the scenario and none is Census data; the integrated EIN filings in Ohio, Pennsylvania and Michigan, and the autumn 2025 rise in applications, are fictional. The company files follow the layouts of a payroll platform's onboarding export, quarterly wage files, state registrations and migration crosswalk, a legacy client system's quarterly wage report and a payroll tax team's successor transfer register. No real organisation's records or person is depicted.

files.source: Constructed in the layout of the Business Formation Statistics monthly download (bfs_monthly.csv, April 2026 release). Every value is simulated for the scenario, the same constructed series as the October pull at an earlier vintage; none is a Census value

files.source: Constructed in the layout of the U.S. Census Bureau's Business Formation Statistics API response (timeseries/eits/bfs, October 2026 release, twelve states, January 2021 to September 2026). Nothing in it is a Census value: every series for every state is simulated for the scenario, and the Ohio, Pennsylvania and Michigan series from 2023 carry the scenario's fictional integrated EIN filings. Only the layout (field names, series codes, FIPS codes, adjustment flags, the formation series' publication lag) follows the real release
